findings.title: Public findMany() API is removed without migrating callers
findings.body: The previous public findMany(findManyArgs) method, which callers used to query BookingTimeStatusDenormalized with authorization and filter conditions applied, is deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions(). No call sites are updated in this PR, so any existing consumer of InsightsBookingService.findMany will fail TypeScript compilation / break at runtime. Either keep a compatible findMany wrapper built on the raw conditions or update all callers in the same PR.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests were deleted while caching remains in the service
findings.body: The PR removes the entire 'Caching' describe block that verified repeated getAuthorizationConditions()/getFilterConditions() calls return cached results, but InsightsBookingService still implements cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions. Nothing now guards against regressions such as stale or incorrectly shared Prisma.Sql conditions, despite the conversion changing the cached value type from Prisma where-input objects to Sql objects.

findings.title: Org-scope SQL expectation depends on unspecified database ordering
findings.body: The org-scope test expects teamIds exactly as [org, team, team2, team3] and userIds exactly as [user, user2, user3] inside ANY(...) arrays. The service builds these arrays from findAllByParentId/findAllByTeamIds results, which have no ORDER BY guarantee, so the exact Prisma.sql equality assertion can fail intermittently under a different database return order even though the authorization semantics are unchanged.
